newsitem.title: USA: FedEx not yet determined cause for crash.
newsitem.headline: FedEx not yet determined cause for crash.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said it has not yet determined the cause of a cargo plane accident that injured five people after a crash landing at Newark International Airport early Thursday morning.
Federal Express said the flight contained about 145,000 pounds of revenue payload, including less than 400 pounds of "routine" hazardous materials.
The company said it is cooperating fully with the National Transportation Safety Board and local law enforcement officers, who are coordinating the investigation.
"They've got investigators on the scene in Newark," said Jess Bunn, a Federal Express spokesman.

He declined to specify the materials the plane was carrying, but a company statement said Federal Express "routinely transports hazardous materials and maintains an in-depth knowledge of all regulations governing these goods."
Bunn also said it was too early to provide an estimate on the financial impact of the accident on the company.
Typical goods carried by Federal Express include computer equipment, textiles, pharmaceuticals and auto parts. Hazardous materials include aerosol cans, gases and dry ice, Bunn said.
The cargo jet was en route from Anchorage, Alaska, when it crash landed at about 0135 EDT/0535 GMT, flipped and burst into flames.
Two FedEx crew members and three passengers escaped by crawling through a cockpit window. All were taken to a New Jersey hospital where they were treated and released.
